A1.justification: Both complete 25-page PDFs describe the same AT-DPT study. The methods, equations, experiments, eight figures, and Appendices A-C can be matched despite the changed title and formatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original AT-DPT and baseline experiments on multi-armed bandits, linear bandits, Darkroom2, and Miniworld, including appendix results and training curves.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds Algorithm Distillation comparisons, training ablations, and attack-budget transfer results.

M1.justification: The DPT architecture, supervised action-prediction loss, attacker optimization, and per-timestep context updates are retained. The new emphasis on a population of attackers clarifies the separate per-task attackers already specified in v2 Section 3.3. The additional training variants are experimental controls.

E1.justification: v3 adds an explicit train-test mismatch scenario: training with attack budget B=1 and evaluating against stronger B=3 and B=5 attacks (Table 7). The environments and budget values themselves were already represented in v2. Miniworld's appearance in the main text is a relocation of existing coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 6 adds Algorithm Distillation trained from TS, modified crUCB, and corrupted modified-crUCB histories, plus an AT-DPT random-attack-training comparator. These extend the bandit comparison while retaining the existing comparator sets elsewhere. PPO was already evaluated in v2 Appendix Table 9.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce training with 10-30% suboptimal demonstrations, random-attack training, different AD source histories, and Btrain=1 versus Btest=1,3,5 evaluation. Section 5.1 specifies replacing selected bandit expert actions with the second-best arm. The established experiments retain their reported metrics, model configurations, horizons, and training budgets.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands the diagnostic evidence: Tables 6 and 10 test dependence on optimal demonstrations, Table 6 tests learned-adversary training against random-noise training, and Table 7 tests transfer from weaker to stronger attacks. v2's budget-sensitivity curves already existed as Figure 8 and are retained as v3 Figure 3.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and 95% confidence intervals calculated as 2×SEM over ten experiment replications. The added tables follow this existing practice; no changed run counts, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial results for AD, suboptimal demonstrations, random-attack training, and budget transfer. Existing bandit values also change: Table 2's AT-DPT (A) uniform-random regret changes from 35.1±8.3 to 41.4±7.3; the appendix AT-DPT self-targeted-attack result at epsilon=0.4 changes from 24.2±1.2 to 23.7±1.8. These are revised reported values without an explanation establishing reruns. Retained linear-bandit and original MDP results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 6 adds a best-response-constrained, bi-level loss formulation and mathematical reasoning linking equilibrium behavior to a corruption-corrected posterior, reward identifiability, and regret. This extends v2's equilibrium setup, but supplies no completed theorem or proof; convergence analysis is deferred.

C1.justification: v3 newly claims, to the authors' knowledge, the first study of reward poisoning in meta-RL and emphasizes the attack setup and learning robust algorithms as the central contribution. The main claims about AT-DPT's robustness in bandits, adaptive attacks, and MDPs remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantial interpretations involving informed task priors and corrected posterior sampling, explains adaptive-versus-non-adaptive training tradeoffs, and discusses relevance to LLM agents using tools or retrieval. It also interprets the new demonstration-quality, random-training, and budget-transfer experiments and identifies unresolved convergence requirements. The Darkroom2 case explanation is retained through relocation.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-availability statement and repository link, AD architecture and AdamW settings, batch size, and an explicit adaptive-setting pretraining runtime. The relocated test algorithm drops v2's comment specifying tasks different from adversarial training; this removes an explicit disclosure without establishing an actual split change.

R1.justification: v3 extends positioning through the meta-RL priority claim, a fuller DPT-versus-AD comparison, and connections to posterior sampling, LLM poisoning, Vintix, and ICPE. It adds corresponding citations and removes Levine et al. (2020). Numerous other reference changes are publication or bibliographic updates to retained works.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, the abstract is condensed, and introduction and related-work passages are edited throughout. The discussion is substantially reorganized into named thematic blocks. Miniworld's description moves into the main text, the Darkroom2 case and test algorithm move to the appendix, and code-availability and impact sections are added.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. Tables gain experimental rows, a new budget-transfer table is added, and existing Miniworld results are redisplayed as main-text Table 5. All eight original figures remain; the budget study and Darkroom2 illustration exchange Figure 3/8 positions.

improvement.justification: The AD comparisons, random-training control, and demonstration-quality and budget-transfer analyses strengthen evidence for the existing claims and partly address v2's reliance on ideal training conditions. Code-access information also improves reproducibility documentation. These are useful targeted gains, limited by the unfinished theoretical argument and unexplained differences between corresponding main-text and appendix bandit scores, including v3 Tables 1 and 6.
